# Velora command reference

Every command is `velora [GLOBAL OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGUMENTS] [OPTIONS]`. Run `velora COMMAND --help` for the same information in the terminal.

## Global options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--site` | site to run the command against (default: VELORA_SITE, `velora use`, or the only site) |
| `--workspace` | workspace directory (default: the nearest parent folder that contains config/apps.txt) |
| `--company` | company id/code (platform mode) to run install-app / migrate / doctypes / backup against |
| `--version` | show program's version number and exit |

Typical day to day: `velora start`, `velora doctor`, `velora ops backup`, `velora update`. Most commands find the workspace from the folder you are in, and the company when there is only one.

## Start here

### `velora quickstart`

Everything, in one step: creates the workspace folder, the control plane (sign-in and companies), a first company with its own database, a sample app and the administrator, then starts the server. If you do not give a password, one is generated and shown once. SQLite by default (for trying things out); use `--db postgres` for real use. Safe to run again in the same folder.

```
velora quickstart [-h] [--email EMAIL] [--password PASSWORD] [--company COMPANY] [--no-sample] [--no-start] [--open] [--port PORT] [--db {sqlite,postgres}] [--db-host DB_HOST] [--db-port DB_PORT] [--db-root-user DB_ROOT_USER] [--db-root-password DB_ROOT_PASSWORD] [path]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | folder for the new workspace |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--email` VALUE |  | the administrator's email address (it is the sign-in) |
| `--password` VALUE |  | default: generated and shown once |
| `--company` VALUE |  | your first company's name |
| `--no-sample` |  | do not create the sample app |
| `--no-start` |  | create everything but do not start the server |
| `--open` |  | open the browser |
| `--port` VALUE | `8000` | port the server listens on |
| `--db` VALUE | `sqlite` | database engine: sqlite (to try things out) or postgres (for real use) |
| `--db-host` VALUE | `localhost` | PostgreSQL host |
| `--db-port` VALUE | `5432` | PostgreSQL port |
| `--db-root-user` VALUE | `postgres` | PostgreSQL administrator that may create databases and users (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_USER) |
| `--db-root-password` VALUE |  | that administrator's password (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD) |

Examples:

```bash
velora quickstart my-erp --email you@company.com
velora quickstart my-erp --email you@company.com --company "Acme Ltd" --no-start
velora quickstart my-erp --email you@company.com --db postgres --db-root-password SECRET
```

### `velora start`

Runs the web server and the Desk (the browser interface), with the background worker (notifications, reminders, scheduled jobs) inside it. Each time it starts it also tidies the folder layout, repairs permissions and upgrades any database that is behind the installed code, so there is nothing else to remember. Behind a web server use the default host (127.0.0.1).

```
velora start [-h] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--no-worker] [--auto-upgrade | --no-auto-upgrade]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` VALUE | `127.0.0.1` | address to listen on (127.0.0.1 = this machine only; 0.0.0.0 = every network) |
| `--port` VALUE | `8000` | port to listen on |
| `--no-worker` |  | do not run the background worker (notifications, reminders, scheduled jobs) inside this server |
| `--auto-upgrade` / `--no-auto-upgrade` |  | upgrade databases that are behind the installed code when the server starts (default: on after `velora quickstart` / the installer) |

Examples:

```bash
velora start
velora start --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
velora start --no-worker
```

### `velora serve`

The same as `velora start` (an alias).

```
velora serve [-h] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--no-worker] [--auto-upgrade | --no-auto-upgrade]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--host` VALUE | `127.0.0.1` | address to listen on (127.0.0.1 = this machine only; 0.0.0.0 = every network) |
| `--port` VALUE | `8000` | port to listen on |
| `--no-worker` |  | do not run the background worker (notifications, reminders, scheduled jobs) inside this server |
| `--auto-upgrade` / `--no-auto-upgrade` |  | upgrade databases that are behind the installed code when the server starts (default: on after `velora quickstart` / the installer) |

Examples:

```bash
velora serve --port 8000
```

### `velora doctor`

Checks the whole installation (Python, operating system, PostgreSQL, folder layout, databases, worker, backups) and says how to fix anything wrong. Exit code 1 if something failed.

```
velora doctor [-h]
```

Examples:

```bash
velora doctor
```

### `velora layout`

Shows the folder structure of this workspace with real sizes, and anything that needs attention (loose permissions, an older layout awaiting its move). `--fix` repairs: older settings files are moved to `config/`, secrets become owner-only, the README and `.gitignore` are refreshed (only if you have not edited them). Exit code 1 if a warning remains.

```
velora layout [-h] [--fix] [--write-docs FILE]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--fix` |  | apply the repairs: move old files into place, make secrets owner-only, refresh README and .gitignore |
| `--write-docs` VALUE |  | (maintainers) write the generated docs/file-structure.md |

Examples:

```bash
velora layout
velora layout --fix
```

## Update, upgrade and recover

### `velora update`

Gets new versions and applies them in one step: new code for apps (from git) and for Velora (from pip, a wheel or git), a backup, the database upgrade on the NEW code, then a restart. If anything fails everything is rolled back. `--check` only lists what is available.

```
velora update [-h] [--check] [--dry-run] [--framework-source FRAMEWORK_SOURCE] [--app APP] [--no-apps] [--partial] [--no-backup] [--restart-command RESTART_COMMAND] [--yes]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--check` |  | only list available updates |
| `--dry-run` |  | show what would happen without changing anything |
| `--framework-source` VALUE |  | where to get velora: a pip spec, a wheel file, a directory of wheels or a git URL |
| `--app` VALUE |  | update only this app |
| `--no-apps` |  | update Velora only, not the apps |
| `--partial` |  | keep going if one database fails; it stays 'upgrade pending' |
| `--no-backup` |  | skip the safety backup that is normally taken first (not recommended) |
| `--restart-command` VALUE |  | run after a successful update, e.g. 'sudo systemctl restart velora' |
| `--yes` |  | do not ask for confirmation |

Examples:

```bash
velora update --check
velora update --yes
velora update --framework-source git+ssh://git@github.com/YOUR-USER/velora.git@main --yes
```

### `velora upgrade`

Upgrades the databases to the code that is installed (migrations and patches), with a backup first and automatic rollback. Use `velora update` to fetch new code as well. `--dry-run` shows the plan without changing anything.

```
velora upgrade [-h] [--dry-run] [--partial] [--no-backup] [--only ONLY] [--force] [--yes] [--report-file REPORT_FILE] [--plan-file PLAN_FILE]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` |  | show what would happen without changing anything |
| `--partial` |  | keep going if one database fails (it stays 'upgrade pending') |
| `--no-backup` |  | skip the safety backup taken before upgrading (not recommended) |
| `--only` VALUE |  | upgrade just this target (control-plane, COMP-001, a site name) |
| `--force` |  | go ahead even if the safety checks object |
| `--yes` |  | do not ask for confirmation |
| `--report-file` VALUE |  | write the report, as JSON, to this file |
| `--plan-file` VALUE |  | require an unchanged, previously reviewed upgrade-plan.json |

Examples:

```bash
velora upgrade --dry-run
velora upgrade --yes
velora upgrade --only COMP-001
```

### `velora upgrade-plan`

Shows what `velora upgrade` WOULD change (schema and patches) without touching any database, and writes a fingerprinted plan file you can review. Pass that file to `velora upgrade --plan-file` to require that nothing changed since you reviewed it.

```
velora upgrade-plan [-h] [--only ONLY] [--out OUT]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--only` VALUE |  | include only this target (control-plane, COMP-001, a site name) |
| `--out` VALUE | `upgrade-plan.json` | write a reviewable fingerprinted plan file |

Examples:

```bash
velora upgrade-plan
velora upgrade-plan --only COMP-001 --out plan.json
```

### `velora restore`

Restores ONE database from a backup file (atomic: all or nothing; a safety copy of the current database is taken first unless told otherwise). For the whole workspace on a new machine use `velora ops restore-workspace`.

```
velora restore [-h] [--company COMPANY] [--control-plane] [--no-safety-backup] [--yes] file
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `file` | the backup file to restore |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--company` VALUE |  | the company to restore it into |
| `--control-plane` |  | restore the control plane (sign-in and company list) instead of a company |
| `--no-safety-backup` |  | do not copy the current database aside before replacing it |
| `--yes` |  | do not ask for confirmation |

Examples:

```bash
velora restore backups/20261111-COMP-001-database.sqlite.gz --company COMP-001 --yes
```

### `velora maintenance`

Turns maintenance mode on or off: the API answers 503 and the Desk shows an upgrading page. Updates do this automatically.

```
velora maintenance [-h] [--message MESSAGE] {on,off,status}
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | on, off, or status One of: on, off, status. |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--message` VALUE |  | text shown to people while maintenance is on |

Examples:

```bash
velora maintenance on --message "Back at 18:00"
velora maintenance off
velora maintenance status
```

## Back up and monitor (`velora ops ...`)

### `velora ops`

Workspace health, encrypted backups, recovery rehearsals, alerts and metrics. The first word after `ops` is the action (table below). Backups are encrypted with a password: give it at the prompt, or in the environment variable VELORA_BACKUP_PASSWORD for cron and services.

```
velora ops [-h] [--into INTO] [--no-files] [--keep KEEP] [--every-hours EVERY_HOURS] [--no-workspace-snapshot] [--no-verify] [--force] [--out OUT] [--format {json,prometheus}] [--email EMAIL] [--webhook WEBHOOK] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--database-url DATABASE_URL] {status,backup,verify,prune,configure,run-scheduled,backup-status,monitor,recovery-report,restore-workspace,rehearse,dashboard,alert-configure,alerts,metrics,notify,serve-dashboard,postgres-rehearse,recovery-assurance} [path]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | what to do (see the table of actions below) One of: status, backup, verify, prune, configure, run-scheduled, backup-status, monitor, recovery-report, restore-workspace, rehearse, dashboard, alert-configure, alerts, metrics, notify, serve-dashboard, postgres-rehearse, recovery-assurance. |
| `path` | backup path for verify, or output path for backup |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--into` VALUE |  | restore-workspace: the NEW directory to restore into |
| `--no-files` |  | backup: leave the uploaded files/ folder out (back it up separately) |
| `--keep` VALUE | `14` | number of newest backups to retain |
| `--every-hours` VALUE | `24` | scheduled backup interval (1–720 hours) |
| `--no-workspace-snapshot` |  | schedule database backups only |
| `--no-verify` |  | skip post-backup integrity checks |
| `--force` |  | run scheduled backups even when not due |
| `--out` VALUE |  | output file for dashboard or metrics |
| `--format` VALUE | `prometheus` | metrics output format |
| `--email` VALUE |  | explicit alert recipient (requires SMTP environment configuration) |
| `--webhook` VALUE |  | explicit HTTPS webhook destination |
| `--host` VALUE | `127.0.0.1` | dashboard bind address; loopback is the safe default |
| `--port` VALUE | `8765` | dashboard port |
| `--database-url` VALUE |  | PostgreSQL URL for isolated restore rehearsal; prefer environment secret |

Examples:

```bash
velora ops status
velora ops backup
velora ops backup --no-files
velora ops verify backups/workspace-20261111T100000Z.vbackup
velora ops restore-workspace backups/workspace-20261111T100000Z.vbackup --into ~/my-erp-restored
velora ops configure --every-hours 24 --keep 14
velora ops run-scheduled
velora ops metrics --format prometheus --out metrics.prom
velora ops alerts
```

### `velora backup`

Backs up the database of a company (or a site) to a compressed file in `backups/`. With `--all`, every company. For the whole workspace (apps, settings, keys, uploads) use `velora ops backup`.

```
velora backup [-h] [--all]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--all` |  | back up every database in the workspace |

Examples:

```bash
velora --company COMP-001 backup
velora backup --all
```

### `velora pg`

PostgreSQL: what this server offers (version, extensions) and how well it is set up; `optimize` applies the safe improvements.

```
velora pg [-h] [--json] [--user USER] [--password-file PASSWORD_FILE] {status,optimize,admin,admin-set}
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | status/optimize: this server; admin: show which PostgreSQL administrator login Velora uses to create companies; admin-set: choose it One of: status, optimize, admin, admin-set. |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` |  | machine-readable (JSON) output |
| `--user` VALUE | `velora_root` | admin-set: the PostgreSQL administrator (installer default velora_root) |
| `--password-file` VALUE |  | admin-set: file that holds that administrator's password (the installer's is <install folder>/.db-root-password) |

Examples:

```bash
velora pg status
velora pg status --json
velora pg optimize
velora pg admin
velora pg admin-set --user velora_root --password-file /srv/velora/.db-root-password
```

### `velora readiness`

Checks that the workspace is configured for production and says what is missing. Exit code 1 if it is not ready.

```
velora readiness [-h]
```

Examples:

```bash
velora readiness
```

### `velora manifest`

Creates, or verifies, a deployment integrity manifest: hashes of the files that matter, with no credentials in it, so you can prove a server still runs exactly what you deployed.

```
velora manifest [-h] {create,verify} [path]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | create a manifest, or verify the current files against one One of: create, verify. |
| `path` | manifest file path (default: config/deployment-manifest.json) |

Examples:

```bash
velora manifest create
velora manifest verify
```

### `velora worker`

Runs the scheduled tasks for every company (notification delivery, reminders, scheduled jobs) on its own, without the web server. `velora start` already runs this inside the server; use it only for a separate worker process.

```
velora worker [-h] [--once] [--interval INTERVAL]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--once` |  | one pass, then exit |
| `--interval` VALUE | `5.0` | seconds to wait between runs |

Examples:

```bash
velora worker
velora worker --once
velora worker --interval 30
```

### `velora ops` actions

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| `status` | A health snapshot as JSON (disk space, logs, apps). Exit code 1 if it fails. |
| `backup [PATH]` | An encrypted backup of the whole workspace: apps, settings, keys, the control plane and company databases (SQLite databases captured consistently), and uploaded files (left out, and the backup says so, above 1 GiB; `--no-files` leaves them out on purpose). PostgreSQL companies are not inside: use `velora backup`. |
| `verify PATH` | Decrypts a backup and checks it: the archive reads end to end and every SQLite database inside passes its integrity check. Works on any machine, with or without a workspace. |
| `restore-workspace PATH --into DIR` | Restores a workspace backup into a NEW folder on a machine that has nothing. Never overwrites; refuses unsafe archives; keys and uploads become owner-only. |
| `prune [--keep N]` | Deletes all but the newest N workspace backups (default 14). |
| `configure` | Sets the backup policy: how often (`--every-hours`), how many to keep (`--keep`), whether to include a workspace snapshot, whether to verify. Then schedule `run-scheduled` with cron or systemd. |
| `run-scheduled [--force]` | Runs the backups that are due (uses VELORA_BACKUP_PASSWORD). Exit code 1 if a backup failed. |
| `backup-status` | When the last backups were made and whether the next one is due. |
| `monitor` | A monitoring snapshot as JSON. Exit code 1 if it fails. |
| `recovery-report` | How old the evidence of a working recovery is. Exit code 1 if it is stale or unknown. |
| `rehearse PATH` | Proves a compressed company database backup can be restored, in a scratch location. |
| `postgres-rehearse PATH [--database-url URL]` | Proves a PostgreSQL dump restores into a disposable database, checks the restored tables against the dump, and records the measured restore time. |
| `recovery-assurance` | The recorded evidence of rehearsals (the measured recovery time; it does not measure how much data a disaster would lose). |
| `dashboard [--out FILE]` | Writes a static HTML operations dashboard. |
| `serve-dashboard [--host H] [--port P]` | Serves a live operations dashboard (loopback only by default; protect it with VELORA_OPS_DASHBOARD_TOKEN if you expose it). |
| `alert-configure` | Creates or shows the alert policy. |
| `alerts` | Evaluates the alerts. Exit code 1 if any is critical. |
| `notify [--email A] [--webhook URL]` | Delivers the current alerts by email (VELORA_SMTP_* settings) or to an HTTPS webhook. |
| `metrics [--format json|prometheus] [--out FILE]` | The metrics, as JSON or in Prometheus text format. |

## Companies, people and access

### `velora platform`

The control plane: central sign-in, tenants and companies. `init` creates it (quickstart does this for you), `status` reports it, `audit` lists its security audit trail.

```
velora platform [-h] {init,status,audit} ...
```

Examples:

```bash
velora platform init --admin-email you@company.com
velora platform status
velora platform audit
```

#### `velora platform init`

Create the control plane (identity + company registry).

```
velora platform init [-h] [--db {sqlite,postgres}] [--db-host DB_HOST] [--db-port DB_PORT] [--db-root-user DB_ROOT_USER] [--db-root-password DB_ROOT_PASSWORD] [--db-name DB_NAME] [--db-user DB_USER] [--db-password DB_PASSWORD] --admin-email ADMIN_EMAIL [--admin-password ADMIN_PASSWORD]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--db` VALUE |  | database engine: sqlite (to try things out) or postgres (for real use) |
| `--db-host` VALUE | `localhost` | PostgreSQL host |
| `--db-port` VALUE | `5432` | PostgreSQL port |
| `--db-root-user` VALUE | `postgres` | PostgreSQL administrator that may create databases and users (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_USER) |
| `--db-root-password` VALUE |  | that administrator's password (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD) |
| `--db-name` VALUE |  | database name to use or create |
| `--db-user` VALUE |  | database user to use or create |
| `--db-password` VALUE |  | that user's password (or VELORA_DB_PASSWORD) |
| `--admin-email` VALUE |  | email of the first platform administrator |
| `--admin-password` VALUE |  | or set VELORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD, or you will be prompted |

#### `velora platform status`

```
velora platform status [-h]
```

#### `velora platform audit`

Recent security events.

```
velora platform audit [-h] [--limit LIMIT]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--limit` VALUE | `20` | how many audit entries to show |

### `velora tenant`

A tenant is a group that owns companies (for example a business group). Companies belong to a tenant.

```
velora tenant [-h] {create,list} ...
```

Examples:

```bash
velora tenant create "Acme Group"
velora tenant list
```

#### `velora tenant create`

```
velora tenant create [-h] name
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | the tenant's name |

#### `velora tenant list`

```
velora tenant list [-h]
```

### `velora company`

A company has its OWN database, apps, users and files: nothing is shared between companies. `create` provisions the database and installs the apps you name; `suspend` blocks access without deleting anything; `drop` removes it permanently (needs `--yes`).

```
velora company [-h] {create,list,suspend,activate,drop} ...
```

Examples:

```bash
velora company create "Acme Ltd" --tenant "Acme Group" --apps velora_notify,velora_search
velora company list
velora company suspend COMP-002
velora company activate COMP-002
```

#### `velora company create`

Provision a company database.

```
velora company create [-h] --tenant TENANT [--code CODE] [--apps APPS] [--db {sqlite,postgres}] [--db-host DB_HOST] [--db-port DB_PORT] [--db-root-user DB_ROOT_USER] [--db-root-password DB_ROOT_PASSWORD] [--db-name DB_NAME] [--db-user DB_USER] [--db-password DB_PASSWORD] name
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | the company's name |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--tenant` VALUE |  | the tenant that owns the company (create it first with `velora tenant create`) |
| `--code` VALUE |  | a short id for the company (default: generated, like COMP-001) |
| `--apps` VALUE | `` | comma-separated apps to install |
| `--db` VALUE |  | database engine: sqlite (to try things out) or postgres (for real use) |
| `--db-host` VALUE | `localhost` | PostgreSQL host |
| `--db-port` VALUE | `5432` | PostgreSQL port |
| `--db-root-user` VALUE |  | PostgreSQL administrator (default: the one the installer set up, see `velora pg admin`) |
| `--db-root-password` VALUE |  | that administrator's password (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD) |
| `--db-name` VALUE |  | database name to use or create |
| `--db-user` VALUE |  | database user to use or create |
| `--db-password` VALUE |  | that user's password (or VELORA_DB_PASSWORD) |

#### `velora company list`

```
velora company list [-h]
```

#### `velora company suspend`

```
velora company suspend [-h] company
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `company` | the company's id |

#### `velora company activate`

```
velora company activate [-h] company
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `company` | the company's id |

#### `velora company drop`

```
velora company drop [-h] [--yes] [--db-root-user DB_ROOT_USER] [--db-root-password DB_ROOT_PASSWORD] company
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `company` | the company's id |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--yes` |  | confirm the permanent removal |
| `--db-root-user` VALUE |  | PostgreSQL administrator that may create databases and users (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_USER) |
| `--db-root-password` VALUE |  | that administrator's password (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD) |

### `velora user`

People who can sign in, and which companies they can use and with which roles. Passwords are never printed; give one with `--password`, the VELORA_USER_PASSWORD variable, or let it be generated.

```
velora user [-h] {create,list,grant,revoke,set-password,deactivate,activate} ...
```

Examples:

```bash
velora user create you@company.com --name "Your Name" --platform-admin
velora user grant you@company.com COMP-001 --roles "System Manager"
velora user list
velora user set-password you@company.com
velora user deactivate old.staff@company.com
```

#### `velora user create`

```
velora user create [-h] [--name NAME] [--platform-admin] [--password PASSWORD] email
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `email` | the person's email address (their sign-in) |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` VALUE | `` | their full name |
| `--platform-admin` |  | make them an administrator of the whole platform |
| `--password` VALUE |  | their first password (or VELORA_USER_PASSWORD; generated and shown once if omitted) |

#### `velora user list`

```
velora user list [-h]
```

#### `velora user grant`

Let a user into a company with roles.

```
velora user grant [-h] --roles ROLES email company
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `email` | the person |
| `company` | the company's id |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--roles` VALUE |  | comma-separated, e.g. 'System Manager,Sales User' |

#### `velora user revoke`

```
velora user revoke [-h] email company
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `email` | the person |
| `company` | the company's id |

#### `velora user set-password`

```
velora user set-password [-h] [--password PASSWORD] email
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `email` | the person |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--password` VALUE |  | the new password (prompted for if omitted) |

#### `velora user deactivate`

```
velora user deactivate [-h] email
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `email` | the person |

#### `velora user activate`

```
velora user activate [-h] email
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `email` | the person |

### `velora domain`

Gives a company its own web address in one step: registers it, configures the web server (nginx) and HTTPS. `check` verifies the DNS, `list` shows the registered addresses, `remove` undoes it.

```
velora domain [-h] [--primary] [--unlocked] [--no-tls] [--dry-run] {add,list,remove,check} [name] [COMPANY]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | what to do with the address One of: add, list, remove, check. |
| `name` | e.g. erp.acme.com |
| `target` | the company id the address belongs to (for add) |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--primary` |  | make this the company's main address |
| `--unlocked` |  | let people on this address reach the user's OTHER companies too |
| `--no-tls` |  | register without HTTPS |
| `--dry-run` |  | show the steps without doing them |

Examples:

```bash
velora domain add erp.acme.com COMP-001
velora domain check erp.acme.com
velora domain list
velora domain remove erp.acme.com
```

## Apps

### `velora new-app`

Scaffolds a new app in `apps/NAME`: a Python package with `hooks.py` and a first module.

```
velora new-app [-h] [--module MODULE] [--title TITLE] name
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | the app's name (a valid Python name) |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--module` VALUE |  | name of the app's first module |
| `--title` VALUE |  | a human-readable title |

Examples:

```bash
velora new-app accounting
velora new-app accounting --title "Accounting"
```

### `velora new-doctype`

Scaffolds one DocType in an app: the JSON definition, a controller and client scripts. `--submittable` adds the draft, submit, cancel life cycle; `--child` makes it a table inside another DocType.

```
velora new-doctype [-h] --app APP [--module MODULE] [--submittable] [--child] name
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | the DocType's name, for example "Journal Entry" |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--app` VALUE |  | the app to put it in |
| `--module` VALUE |  | module (folder) inside the app |
| `--submittable` |  | make it submittable (draft, submit, cancel) |
| `--child` |  | child table DocType |

Examples:

```bash
velora new-doctype "Journal Entry" --app accounting --submittable
```

### `velora new-doctypes`

Creates DocTypes in an app from a JSON file, either Velora's own format or a Frappe DocType export. `--dry-run` shows what would happen; `--on-conflict` decides what to do when one exists.

```
velora new-doctypes [-h] [--module MODULE] [--name NAME] [--child] [--submittable] [--track-changes] [--autoname-field AUTONAME_FIELD] [--on-conflict {error,skip}] [--dry-run] app file
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app` | the app to add the DocTypes to |
| `file` | a JSON file, or - for standard input |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--module` VALUE |  | module inside the app to put them in |
| `--name` VALUE |  | the DocType name, when the JSON is only a list of fields |
| `--child` |  | create them as child tables (rows inside another DocType) |
| `--submittable` |  | make them submittable (draft, submit, cancel) |
| `--track-changes` |  | keep a version history of every change |
| `--autoname-field` VALUE |  | name documents after this field |
| `--on-conflict` VALUE | `error` | what to do with a DocType that already exists |
| `--dry-run` |  | validate and show what would be created, write nothing |

Examples:

```bash
velora new-doctypes accounting exported.json --dry-run
velora new-doctypes accounting exported.json --module Accounts
```

### `velora get-app`

Clones an app from git into `apps/`. It does not install it: use `install-app`.

```
velora get-app [-h] [--name NAME] [--branch BRANCH] url
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `url` | the git URL of the app |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` VALUE |  | the folder name to use under apps/ |
| `--branch` VALUE |  | the branch or tag to clone |

Examples:

```bash
velora get-app https://github.com/YOUR-USER/myapp.git --branch main
```

### `velora list-apps`

Lists the apps in this workspace.

```
velora list-apps [-h]
```

Examples:

```bash
velora list-apps
```

### `velora validate-app`

Validates an app package WITHOUT running its code.

```
velora validate-app [-h] app
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app` | the app to check (its folder name) |

Examples:

```bash
velora validate-app accounting
```

### `velora export-app`

Builds a verified, distributable ZIP of an app (with a manifest of hashes).

```
velora export-app [-h] [--output OUTPUT] app
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app` | the app to package (its folder name) |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--output` VALUE |  | output ZIP path (default: workspace/dist/<app>-<version>.zip) |

Examples:

```bash
velora export-app accounting --output accounting.zip
```

### `velora import-app-package`

Validates a Velora app ZIP and adds it to this workspace. It rejects unsafe archives (paths that escape, links, undeclared files). It does not install the app.

```
velora import-app-package [-h] [--overwrite] package
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `package` | path of the app ZIP |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--overwrite` |  | replace existing app source after validating the archive |

Examples:

```bash
velora import-app-package accounting.zip
```

### `velora marketplace`

Trusted local repositories of validated app packages (ZIP files). Add a folder as a source, list sources, and import a package from one, optionally checking its SHA-256 digest. Importing adds the app to the workspace; it does not install it.

```
velora marketplace [-h] [--sha256 SHA256] [--overwrite] {list,add-source,remove-source,import} [name] [value]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | list sources, add or remove a trusted source, or import a package from one One of: list, add-source, remove-source, import. |
| `name` | repository name |
| `value` | repository directory or package ZIP filename |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--sha256` VALUE |  | expected package SHA-256 digest |
| `--overwrite` |  | replace existing app source after validation |

Examples:

```bash
velora marketplace list
velora marketplace add-source team /srv/packages
velora marketplace import team my-app.zip --sha256 DIGEST
```

### `velora deploy`

Promotes validated apps from one workspace to another (for example staging to production). Create a profile with the source and target, preview with `plan`, then `promote`; databases are backed up first.

```
velora deploy [-h] [--source SOURCE] [--target TARGET] [--app APP] [--out OUT] [--dry-run] [--yes] {profile-create,profile-list,plan,promote} [name]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | create or list deployment profiles, preview a promotion (plan) or carry it out (promote) One of: profile-create, profile-list, plan, promote. |
| `name` | deployment profile name |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--source` VALUE |  | source workspace path |
| `--target` VALUE |  | target workspace path |
| `--app` VALUE |  | application to promote (repeat for multiple apps) |
| `--out` VALUE |  | write deployment plan/report JSON to this path |
| `--dry-run` |  | preview promotion without changing target |
| `--yes` |  | confirm database backups and application installation |

Examples:

```bash
velora deploy profile-create prod --source /srv/staging --target /srv/prod
velora deploy plan prod --app my-app
velora deploy promote prod --app my-app --yes
```

### `velora install-app`

Installs an app on EVERY company in one step: fetches it (a name in `apps/`, or a git URL), installs its Python packages and required apps first, creates the tables, runs the app's install code and restarts the server. A failure in one company is reported and does not stop the others.

```
velora install-app [-h] [--name NAME] [--branch BRANCH] [--no-deps] [--no-restart] APP
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app` | an app name, a built-in app, a git URL or a folder |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` VALUE |  | app name when it cannot be derived from the URL/folder |
| `--branch` VALUE |  | branch or tag, when the app is fetched from git |
| `--no-deps` |  | do not install Python packages automatically (fail instead) |
| `--no-restart` |  | do not restart the server afterwards |

Examples:

```bash
velora install-app accounting
velora install-app https://github.com/YOUR-USER/governmentone.git --branch main
```

### `velora uninstall-app`

Removes an app from EVERY company in one step, after checking nothing else depends on it, and after a backup. The app's data is kept unless you say `--purge` (which needs the backup).

```
velora uninstall-app [-h] [--purge] [--remove-code] [--no-backup] [--no-restart] [--yes] app
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `app` | the app to remove |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--purge` |  | also DELETE the app's data (a backup is always taken first) |
| `--remove-code` |  | also delete the app's folder from the workspace |
| `--no-backup` |  | skip the backup taken first (the app's data cannot then be purged) |
| `--no-restart` |  | do not restart the server afterwards |
| `--yes` |  | do not ask for confirmation |

Examples:

```bash
velora uninstall-app accounting
velora uninstall-app accounting --purge --yes
```

### `velora deps`

Optional Python packages (data analysis, PDF and QR codes, machine learning, SFTP ...), checked and installed by name.

```
velora deps [-h] [--app APP] [--dry-run] [--upgrade] [--yes] {list,check,install} [extras ...]
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `action` | what to do with the optional packages One of: list, check, install. |
| `extras` | e.g. pdf data ml (or: all) |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--app` VALUE |  | install the packages an app declares (required_packages in its hooks.py) |
| `--dry-run` |  | show what pip would install without installing |
| `--upgrade` |  | also upgrade packages that are already installed |
| `--yes` |  | install without asking |

Examples:

```bash
velora deps list
velora deps check pdf
velora deps install pdf data
```

## Data

### `velora import-data`

Loads any DocType's data from an Excel, CSV or JSON file. Columns are matched by name in any order; child rows go on the lines under their document. `--dry-run` runs the real validation and SAVES NOTHING. Modes: insert, update, upsert. `--atomic` imports all or nothing. See docs/data-import.md.

```
velora import-data [-h] [--mode {insert,update,upsert}] [--dry-run] [--submit] [--atomic] [--keep-names] [--date-format {DMY,MDY,YMD}] [--match MATCH] [--report REPORT] [--max-rows MAX_ROWS] doctype file
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `doctype` | the DocType to import into |
| `file` | the .xlsx, .csv or .json file to import |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--mode` VALUE | `insert` | insert (create new documents), update (change existing ones) or upsert (both) |
| `--dry-run` |  | check the file with the real validation and save nothing |
| `--submit` |  | submit submittable documents after creating them |
| `--atomic` |  | all or nothing: if any document fails, nothing is imported |
| `--keep-names` |  | keep the IDs in the file (migration; System Manager) |
| `--date-format` VALUE | `DMY` | how dates are written in the file: DMY (31/12/2026), MDY (12/31/2026) or YMD (2026-12-31) |
| `--match` VALUE |  | update/upsert: find existing documents by this unique field instead of the ID |
| `--report` VALUE |  | write the failed rows (with the reason) to this CSV file |
| `--max-rows` VALUE | `200000` | refuse a file with more documents than this |

Examples:

```bash
velora import-data Customer customers.xlsx --dry-run
velora import-data Customer customers.xlsx --report failed.csv
velora import-data Customer changes.csv --mode update
```

### `velora export-data`

Exports a DocType's data as JSON, CSV or Excel in exactly the layout `import-data` reads, to move data between companies or servers.

```
velora export-data [-h] [--format {json,csv,xlsx}] [--out OUT] [--filters FILTERS] [--limit LIMIT] doctype
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `doctype` | the DocType to export |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--format` VALUE | `json` | json, csv or xlsx (all can be imported again) |
| `--out` VALUE |  | file to write (default: a name made from the DocType and the time) |
| `--filters` VALUE |  | JSON, e.g. [["status","=","Active"]] |
| `--limit` VALUE | `50000` | most entries to show or export |

Examples:

```bash
velora export-data Customer --format json --out customers.json
velora export-data Customer --format csv --filters '[["status","=","Active"]]'
```

### `velora import-template`

Writes a blank import file with the right headings (and, for Excel, an Instructions sheet).

```
velora import-template [-h] [--format {xlsx,csv}] [--out OUT] doctype
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `doctype` | the DocType to make a template for |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--format` VALUE | `xlsx` | xlsx (with an Instructions sheet) or csv |
| `--out` VALUE |  | file to write (default: a name made from the DocType and the time) |

Examples:

```bash
velora import-template "Sales Order" --format xlsx
```

### `velora migrate`

Brings a database in line with the installed apps' DocTypes (tables and columns). Upgrades and `install-app` do this for you; use it directly when you are developing. `--dry-run` prints the plan.

```
velora migrate [-h] [--dry-run] [--all-companies]
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` |  | print the plan without changing the database |
| `--all-companies` |  | platform mode: migrate every active company database |

Examples:

```bash
velora migrate --dry-run
velora migrate --all-companies
```

### `velora doctypes`

Lists a database's DocTypes.

```
velora doctypes [-h]
```

Examples:

```bash
velora --company COMP-001 doctypes
```

## Older one-database-per-site mode

### `velora init`

Creates an empty workspace folder (the older step-by-step flow). `velora quickstart` does this and much more.

```
velora init [-h] path
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `path` | folder to create the workspace in |

Examples:

```bash
velora init my-erp
```

### `velora new-site`

Older mode: creates one site with its own database. New installations use companies instead.

```
velora new-site [-h] [--db {sqlite,postgres}] [--db-host DB_HOST] [--db-port DB_PORT] [--db-root-user DB_ROOT_USER] [--db-root-password DB_ROOT_PASSWORD] [--db-name DB_NAME] [--db-user DB_USER] [--db-password DB_PASSWORD] [--developer-mode] name
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | the site's name |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--db` VALUE |  | default: postgres if root/db credentials are given, else sqlite (development) |
| `--db-host` VALUE | `localhost` | PostgreSQL host |
| `--db-port` VALUE | `5432` | PostgreSQL port |
| `--db-root-user` VALUE | `postgres` | PostgreSQL administrator that may create databases and users (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_USER) |
| `--db-root-password` VALUE |  | Velora creates a role + database for the site |
| `--db-name` VALUE |  | existing database (managed hosting) |
| `--db-user` VALUE |  | existing database user |
| `--db-password` VALUE |  | that user's password (or VELORA_DB_PASSWORD) |
| `--developer-mode` |  | enable header-based dev sign-in (NEVER in production) |

Examples:

```bash
velora new-site erp.local
```

### `velora drop-site`

Older mode: deletes a site (and its database if Velora created it).

```
velora drop-site [-h] [--db-root-user DB_ROOT_USER] [--db-root-password DB_ROOT_PASSWORD] [--yes] name
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | the site to delete |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--db-root-user` VALUE | `postgres` | PostgreSQL administrator that may create databases and users (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_USER) |
| `--db-root-password` VALUE |  | that administrator's password (or VELORA_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD) |
| `--yes` |  | do not ask for confirmation |

Examples:

```bash
velora drop-site erp.local --yes
```

### `velora list-sites`

Older mode: lists sites.

```
velora list-sites [-h]
```

Examples:

```bash
velora list-sites
```

### `velora use`

Older mode: sets the default site.

```
velora use [-h] name
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | the site to use by default |

Examples:

```bash
velora use erp.local
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `VELORA_WORKSPACE` | the workspace folder (instead of `--workspace` or finding it from the current folder) |
| `VELORA_SITE` | the default site (older mode) |
| `VELORA_MASTER_KEY` | the key that encrypts stored company database passwords; if unset it is kept in `platform/master.key` |
| `VELORA_BACKUP_PASSWORD` | the backup encryption password, for unattended `ops backup`, `verify`, `restore-workspace`, `run-scheduled` |
| `VELORA_ADMIN_PASSWORD / VELORA_USER_PASSWORD` | default password for `quickstart` / `user create` (otherwise generated and shown once) |
| `VELORA_DB_HOST, VELORA_DB_PORT, VELORA_DB_ROOT_USER, VELORA_DB_ROOT_PASSWORD, VELORA_DB_PASSWORD` | PostgreSQL connection defaults for provisioning |
| `VELORA_DB_URL, VELORA_APPS, VELORA_DEVELOPER_MODE` | library/development mode: a database URL, the apps to load, developer mode |
| `VELORA_MAX_BODY_MB` | largest request body the server accepts (default 8; uploads and data imports have their own higher limits) |
| `VELORA_FILE_ROOT` | where uploaded files are stored outside a workspace |
| `VELORA_SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/FROM` | outgoing email for alerts |
| `VELORA_INTEGRATION_MASTER_KEY` | encrypts webhook secrets |
| `VELORA_OPS_DASHBOARD_TOKEN, VELORA_POSTGRES_REHEARSAL_URL, VELORA_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, VELORA_FRONTEND_DIST` | operations dashboard token; the disposable PostgreSQL for restore rehearsals; alert webhook token; a custom Desk build folder |
